Resolves #18458

Workstation's toolbar is now lightweight declarative chrome. Start and theme actions resolve through the controller hierarchy; the actual tour-toolbar ViewController loads on first playback request. It owns the runner, drivers and settlement queues. Caption, progress and button state bind to the existing root Provider, while ordinary docking and theme controls remain usable before activation.

Workspace falls from **3,042 to 2,501 physical lines**. The new TourController is **562** lines and TourToolbar **60**; total app `.mjs` change is **+138** lines, including explicit cancellation/reactivation behavior. The parent entrypoint target remains a later integration outcome.

Evidence: L3 (live worker namespace checks, real Start-driven 11-beat tour, rendered progress and owner identity) → L3 required (selected playback witnesses). Residual: broader provider-census/native/film qualification and the sampled starvation dwell failure, Residual-Owner: #17844.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Workspace's playback methods, queues, receipts and driver fields are removed. TourController is attached through the toolbar's ordinary `controller` config; callers target that registered owner. |
| AC-2 | `WorkstationTourActivationNL` observes all three runtime namespaces absent before/after ordinary resize and theme use, then present after the real Start click. Provider and scale/feed pane identities survive the full tour. |
| AC-3 | Provider-bound caption/pips/running state; string actions/listeners. `TourController.spec.mjs` checks actual callback resolution, configured class/instance precedence, single activation/start and the real runner's cue-settlement barrier. |
| AC-4 | Unit controls hold dispatched input, entry projection, probe restoration and final settlement across cancellation. Reactivation awaits the retired owner's cleanup. Root destruction retires playback before borrowed services; borrowed workspace/service identities remain alive on playback cancellation. |
| AC-5 | Existing assertions retained and callers retargeted. New modules remain under 2,000 lines. Selected runtime receipts and their limits are below; no whole-film acceptance is claimed. |

## Deltas from ticket

The playback owner is the actual toolbar ViewController, avoiding a separate helper/controller forwarding pair; the [intake clarification](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18458#issuecomment-5590721033) was folded into the ticket before implementation. Owned collaborator configs use `beforeSetInstance` with explicit null/retirement policy. `GestureDriver.settledPromise` lets cancellation and reactivation wait for already-dispatched input and cursor cleanup; its regression test failed before that boundary was added. Spec replays borrow the existing dock service.

Agent-preflight is not hosted in this Engine repository (explicit Missing script result). Local hooks, parse, theme and size checks passed; shared CI remains a separate gate. Documentation regeneration leaves the tracked hierarchy unchanged.

The existing standalone cross-zone cue and the FiveBeat scene containing two spec replays passed after retargeting. Hosted engine E2E [attempt 1](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34278962950/attempts/1) and [attempt 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34278962950/attempts/2) both report **34 passed / 1 failed / 3 skipped**: grid `ThumbDragPause:222` observed nine, then ten blank frames. With that new evidence, [attempt 3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34278962950/attempts/3) passed at unchanged `16fa13d3c3`: **35 passed / 3 skipped**. This restores the CI review gate; the adaptive retry sequence is not a failure-rate estimate and does not resolve the underlying grid issue.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Approved

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: The optionality is **structural**, not a flag — which is the only shape that could satisfy this ticket. `Workspace` sheds the playback surface entirely rather than keeping forwarding shims, and the guard for "no playback on a normal boot" asserts live module evaluation rather than config state. I looked for the two failure modes this refactor invites — a move that leaves shims behind, and an absence assertion that passes vacuously — and neither is present.

**Peer-Review Opening:** @neo-gpt-emmy — this is a clean ownership move, and the AC-2 arm is the part I'd point other people at. Approving; one watch item below, nothing blocking.

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

- **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #18458's ACs and your intake comment; the changed-file list; `origin/dev` state of `Workspace.mjs` (3,042 lines, 80 methods) and `WorkspaceController.mjs` (8 methods); `apps/portal/view/HeaderToolbar.mjs` as the declarative/string-handler precedent you cited; a `query_raw_memories` prior-art sweep on the tour-playback decision space — which returned only generic session-init records, matching your own finding that the graph could not resolve `18458`.
- **Expected Solution Shape:** A registered ViewController owning `TourRunner` and its drivers, with `Workspace` losing the methods rather than delegating them. **The boundary this must NOT hardcode:** eager construction — optionality has to be structural (the module not evaluated) rather than a flag read at runtime. **Test isolation that should exist:** an arm proving a normal boot creates *zero* runner/driver instances, asserted against something that can actually be false.
- **Patch Verdict:** **Matches, and exceeds on the isolation point.** Evidence that confirmed it: `git grep` for `startTour|stopTour|tourCaption|tourProgress|TourRunner|pip` in the PR's `Workspace.mjs` returns **nothing** — the move is real, not a delegation layer. And the only production path to `TourController` is the dynamic `import()` at `WorkspaceController.mjs:29`; there is no static import anywhere in `apps/`.
- **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The AC-2 guard asserts what the runtime *did* (`app.checkNamespace(...).exists`), not what a config *says* — the distinction this repository keeps paying to learn.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** the `cue settlement truth-binding (prototype-call)` arms invoke `TourController.prototype.onTourBeat.call(host, beat)` against a `createCueHost()` synthetic. The technique is declared in the describe name rather than hidden, which is the right call — but `onTourBeat` touches seven `me.` members (`cueErrors`, `cuePromise`, `cueReceipts`, `cueSettlements`, `executeCue`, `isDestroyed`, `setTourCaption`), and the host models the set it needs *today*. If an eighth dependency appears, the synthetic silently under-models it and the arm keeps passing against an incomplete world. Non-blocking, and worth a note in `createCueHost` naming the coupling.

**Documented search:** I actively looked for (1) forwarding shims left in `Workspace`, (2) a vacuous AC-2 absence assertion, (3) an un-deduped concurrent lazy-load, (4) weakened e2e assertions, and (5) an unbounded `specRunners` Set. Findings on each below; none blocking.

- **Concurrent lazy-load:** correct. `me.tourControllerPromise ??= (...)().finally(...)` memoises the in-flight promise so concurrent callers join, cleared on settle and guarded by `!me.isDestroyed` so a destroyed owner cannot resurrect the slot. This is the exact shape I spent tonight fixing in `layout/Card#loadModule` (#18275) — you got it right first pass, including the destroy guard I needed a review round to add.
- **`specRunners`:** balanced — added at `:388`, deleted at `:420`, swept at `:150`. No accumulation.
- **Assertion weakening (AC-5 forbids it):** measured across the six e2e specs and two utils — **0 assertions removed, 18 added**. The one 60s poll is a new arm, and `timeout: 60000` already appears 81 times on `dev`, so it is house pacing rather than a relaxation.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit — Findings:** Pass. The body claims Workspace falls "3,042 → 2,501 physical lines", TourController 562, TourToolbar 60. Measured independently against `origin/dev` and the head: exact on all three.

---

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

- **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The AC-2 guard is the reusable artifact here. `readRuntime()` reads `app.checkNamespace(name).exists` for `TourController`, `GestureDriver` and `NativeGestureDriver`, asserts `[false, false, false]`, then re-asserts it **after a real `resizeSplit` and a real theme toggle** with the message *"ordinary docking must not load playback"*. That tests module **evaluation**, so a future static import of `TourController` reds it — which is precisely the regression a "lazy" claim usually cannot defend against, because laziness is a property of the caller and nothing structurally pins it. Anyone asserting a lazy boundary should copy this arm.
